Input O2 line blocked - low pressure
Input O2 line pressure too high

weaknesses: Expected results are often vague; they should assert specific alarm messages, severity, and presence/absence of alarms.
Negative test cases incorrectly expect alarms; they should assert no alarm for values above thresholds.
The test suite uses placeholder "as specified" for O2 line pressure; a concrete threshold should be defined and tested.
No tests assert that the GUI remains silent when unresponsive time is below half the apnea time.
The overpressure alarm tests for the controller at the threshold (60 cmH2O) should assert that no alarm is triggered.

artifact:
Feature: Alarms - Unit U02_Alarms

  Scenario: Air Line Blocked - Low Pressure Alarm
    Given the air line is blocked
    When the device is operating
    Then a HIGH severity alarm "Input air line blocked - low pressure" is triggered in the GUI

  Scenario: O2 Line Blocked - Low Pressure Alarm
    Given the O2 line is blocked
    When the device is operating
    Then a HIGH severity alarm "Input O2 line blocked - low pressure" is triggered in the GUI

  Scenario Outline: Inspiratory Pressure Drop Alarm
    Given the inspiratory pressure is <pressure> cm H2O
    When the device is operating
    Then an alarm is triggered if the inspiratory pressure drops below -4 cm H2O
    Examples:
      | pressure |
      | -3      |
      | -4      |
      | -5      |
      | -10     |

  Scenario: O2 Line Pressure Too High Alarm
    Given the input O2 line pressure is <pressure>
    When the device is operating
    Then a HIGH severity alarm "Input O2 line pressure too high" is triggered if the pressure exceeds as specified

  Scenario Outline: GUI Unresponsive Alarm - Apnea Time
    Given the apnea time is <apnea_time> seconds
    When the GUI is unresponsive for <unresponsive_time> seconds
    Then an alarm is triggered if the unresponsive time is greater than or equal to 1/2 of the apnea time
    Examples:
      | apnea_time | unresponsive_time |
      | 10         | 4                |
      | 10         | 5                |
      | 10         | 6                |
      | 20         | 9                |
      | 20         | 10               |
      | 20         | 11               |

  Scenario: GUI Displays Overpressure Alarm
    Given an overpressure condition exists
    When the device is operating
    Then the GUI displays an overpressure alarm

  Scenario: Controller Unresponsive Alarm - Apnea Time
    Given the apnea time is <apnea_time> seconds
    When the controller is unresponsive for <unresponsive_time> seconds
    Then an alarm is triggered if the unresponsive time is greater than or equal to 1/2 of the apnea time
    Examples:
      | apnea_time | unresponsive_time |
      | 10         | 4                |
      | 10         | 5                |
      | 10         | 6                |
      | 20         | 9                |
      | 20         | 10               |
      | 20         | 11               |

  Scenario Outline: Controller Overpressure Alarm
    Given the inspiratory pressure is <pressure> cmH2O
    When the device is operating
    Then an overpressure alarm is triggered if the pressure exceeds 60 cmH2O
    Examples:
      | pressure |
      | 59       |
      | 60       |
      | 61       |
      | 70       |
